paper_title: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Detection Using Hypercomplex Neural Networks
core_problem: Diagnosis of acute lymphoblast leukemia (ALL) from blood smear digital microscopic images by classifying lymphocytes.
methodology_summary: Utilizing eight hypercomplex-valued convolutional neural networks (HvCNNs) based on hypercomplex algebras (including Clifford algebras) alongside real-valued convolutional networks for image classification.
empirical_results: The HvCNN based on Clifford algebras processing HSV-encoded images achieved an average accuracy rate of 96.6% on the ALL-IDB2 dataset (50% train-test split), outperforming real-valued models with a simpler architecture and fewer parameters.
explicit_limitations: One specific HvCNN based on the algebra B[-1, +1] yielded a median accuracy rate of 93.8% when processing HSV-encoded images, which was lower than other models in the HSV case.
